prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional small molecules direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove a chosen protein.

statement.case_for: Round 1 did not change my preferred configuration: B067 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The decisive point is still that a simple principle, event-driven removal of a protein by a small molecule that recruits an E3 ligase, created a capability that did not exist, and that it has been reproduced independently across many ligases and targets. Crews and Deshaies hold the concept (2001) and every proposer names them. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned the concept into rational, drug-like design, which is the part a chemistry citation can defend as a chemical advance. Five members prefer B067 and two more list it first among alternatives, but I give that count no weight of its own. What I weigh is that the claim is checkable, defined at the molecular level and explainable in one sentence.
statement.case_against: The reservations remain real and I do not think round 1 dissolved them. No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so impact is partly projected. The cereblon and glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim) is not covered by a three-name PROTAC citation, and the committee should state openly that it is excluding people with serious claims. Aili's question about how much of the chemistry is new beyond linker and ligand optimisation is fair; my answer is that the new thing is the design principle, not the linker chemistry. Finally, I must acknowledge that my own first-place opening candidate was B049, so a prize for a drug modality over a physical principle is a choice that I make deliberately.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Crews and Deshaies but names Handa rather than Ciulli, arguing that cereblon identification explains the clinically most advanced degrader and glue class and gave the field its second E3 handle.
responses.response: This is the question that decides the configuration, and I have weighed it again. Handa's identification of cereblon is a clear mechanistic discovery, and I would not call it a footnote. But it explains how an existing drug works, whereas the prize I am proposing rewards building a degrader on purpose against any target. That design capability rests on Crews and Deshaies for the concept and Ciulli for making it rational, with VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures. I therefore keep Ciulli. Your point does change my citation: I now phrase it around directing the ubiquitin-proteasome system, not around PROTAC peptides, so that it does not read as if the glue branch were disproved. I would accept Handa if you can show that the cereblon route, not the VHL route, is the centre of gravity of what chemists now do, but I have not seen that argued.

responses.point: Aili asks how much of degrader chemistry is new beyond linker and ligand optimisation around an existing biological mechanism, and whether the glue and PROTAC strands can share three names.
responses.response: I take the novelty question seriously because it is the strongest internal objection to B067. My answer is that the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery existed, but nobody had used a small molecule to impose proximity between an E3 ligase and a protein chosen in advance, and that is a design principle that changes which proteins are addressable, including those without a druggable pocket. Linker optimisation is refinement; the principle is not. On the glue branch, I agree with your round-1 reply to Chabes that the honest route is to say explicitly what the citation covers and not to swap names silently. I accept that the three-name limit forces a cut, and I would record in the committee's own notes that Handa and Ito have a serious claim on the glue story.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B013 (Buchwald, Hartwig) for maturity, wide use and a clean two-person credit, and answers the 2010 overlap objection by saying C-N coupling needed its own ligand design and mechanistic work.
responses.response: Your answer to the 2010 objection moved me part of the way: most Nobel-level methods build on earlier ones, and C-N coupling did require distinct ligand and mechanistic work, so I no longer treat it as merely incremental. I still rank it behind B067, because it makes an already-possible bond formation general and routine whereas degraders add a new kind of action, removal of a protein. It remains my first fallback if B067 cannot settle its names, and I have moved it to the head of my alternatives for that reason. I would ask you directly: if B067 required excluding the glue branch, would you vote for it, or does the missing approved drug still keep you at B013?

responses.point: Sparr prefers B049 and argues that the artefact concern bears on the citation wording rather than on whether phase separation is ready, and asks whether Rosen or Pappu and Mittag should stand beside Hyman and Brangwynne.
responses.response: We both come from Lund, and I agree with you that our agreement should not count twice. Your argument that the artefact concern bears on wording is the best case for B049 and I considered it again. A citation limited to liquid-like demixing as an organising mechanism would be defensible, but the question of which in-cell assemblies are genuinely phase-separated is, for me, still part of what has been demonstrated, not only of how it is phrased. That is why I keep B049 as an alternative and not as the lead. As for credit, I would favour Rosen over Pappu or Mittag only if the citation emphasises multivalent interactions; the quantitative physical-chemistry side is a harder allocation that I cannot resolve from the file.

responses.point: Zou supports B067 with Ciulli, Crews and Deshaies on condition that the citation is framed around PROTAC design and does not try to cover molecular glues, and is uncertain about the current clinical status of degraders.
responses.response: I agree with the condition in substance: a citation should not claim more than three names can support. I differ in one respect, since I phrase it as directing the ubiquitin-proteasome system, which is accurate for the trio without asserting that glues are covered. On clinical status, I share your uncertainty and I do not want the committee to treat a recalled status as fact. My position is that the mechanism has been independently reproduced, so approval would strengthen the case but its absence should not by itself decide the matter.

uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues are one achievement or two; I treat them as converging on one principle but the committee has not settled it.
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader makes recognition early in 2026; my recollection of current clinical status is not verified.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the correct third name; this is a judgment about which discovery defines the generalisable chemistry.
Whether B049 could carry a narrow citation that survives the artefact critique; I currently think not this year.
My attribution history rests on recall and not on independent verification.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have no known collaboration with or institutional tie to any named candidate on the shortlist, and none is from Lund or NanoLund. I am the chair and a physicist, and Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues, which is a general connection and not a recusal matter. I disclose that my own opening first-place candidate was B049, and that I have now ranked B067 above it on maturity and evidence.
